What diet plan do you follow? Share here!

1. I eat high carb low fat and track my calories and macros on MyFitnessPal. Right now, I'm somewhere in between 70-80% carbs, 10-15% fat, and 10-15% protein, depending on what I eat that day and what my workouts are like.

  2. My success is primarily how I feel. I have more energy, I have less cravings when I'm eating a lot of fruit, I can eat after a workout without feeling sick or gross, and I have had weight loss success, primarily because I have no cravings to eat junk food, which has been my downfall in the past.

  3. Standard day of eating for me is a lot of fruit and starches. I haven't tracked in a while (I need to get back in the habit of doing that), but staples in my diet are rice, quinoa, potatoes, bananas, apples, lettuce, frozen veggies, and smoothies. I eat about 1800 calories a day, primarily fruit and bananas. I use very, very little oil (when I do use it, it's a little spritz of oil for taste) and I avoid other processed fats. I do eat healthy fats in moderation, like flaxseed, raw nuts, and avocado, as well as tofu on occasion, but the bulk of my food comes from fruits, grains, and starches.

  4. My favorite foods are probably bananas and potatoes. The foods I don't eat as much are any oils, and I limit my intake of nuts, avocados, and tofu.

  5. Some famous people who follow and advocate a high carb low fat vegan diet are Joel Fuhrman, Dean Ornish, Neal Barnard, Rip Esselstyn (The Engine 2 Diet), and T. Colin Campbell. This diet is also popular with vegan bodybuilder and fitness enthusiasts, like Robert Cheeke (Vegan Bodybuilding) and Crissi Carvalho (VeganFitnessModel). You've also probably heard of "carbing the fuck up" from Freelee the Banana Girl and other raw or semi-raw vegans (FullyRaw by Kristina, Raw Till 4, etc).

  6. For a beginner or someone curious to try out the diet, I would hope that you like a lot of fruit and that you like to eat a lot! I would recommend counting your calories so you make sure that you eat enough, and just start by eating a lot of your favorite fruits, veggies, and starches. If you have health concerns, I'd recommend reading anything by Joel Fuhrman, who really addresses the benefits of a low-fat vegan diet for health.

  7. In a restaurant, I'm sure it's pretty much the same as any vegan: find out what's on the menu and try to veganize it! Salad is of course always a good bet, but if I can get a plain baked potato or steamed veggies, I'm happy. Veggie sushi is my favorite option though, since it's my ultimate HCLF meal: plenty of rice, veggies, and a little bit of avocado for flavor and creaminess.

  8. I've already mentioned some of my favorite reading material from Joel Fuhrman, but I'd also recommend Happy Herbivore and Appetite for Reduction cookbooks, as they all focus on low-fat meals, and Appetite for Reduction even has nutritional breakdowns for each recipe.

Given the server capacity issues in play here, I have a suggestion for voat.co to consider.

Seek to port your code to a hosting provider, or multiple providers, such as AWS, or in this case, Azure may be a good option as well. In any case, tie the donation system to server auto provisioning. This would require a voat-drone version of code that can be quickly spun up or down without admin action. Tied to a donation system, voat could literally scale up or down based on a combination of load/need and donations/ad-revenue.

Being in IT myself, this is precisely the sort of solution that is used to solve problems like this in modern web apps. Building brick and mortar servers that you have to pay for regardless of load limits your ability to respond to spikes in demand, and also forces you to adopt a fixed cost you may not need if/when traffic subsides.
